focus: Waterfall lane strokes and tap assist

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged exact-Godot 4.7.2 headless probe passed checks for the live cleanup controller's waterfall stage, a downward synthetic touch/drag/release through _gui_input, all three lane clears, progress persistence and unlock, plus standalone tap-assist, same-lane retap, retarget, cancellation, local-contact and touch-owner assertions. The focused source traces these mechanics to the visible waterfall fixture and connects progress/completion to the controller.
route_status.gaps: The probe directly constructs ReefMain, a Control host, and synthetic waterfall/seahorse fixture sprites (scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:29-64), then directly calls the waterfall's _gui_input handler with synthetic events (scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:223-258). It does not enter from the castle through displayed controls or exercise normal engine input routing on a rendered screen. The lane hit geometry, actual visual legibility, spoken playback, physical phone response and observed child comprehension/appeal remain unproven.

code_constants: GUIDE_IDLE_SECONDS=0.6 s before the guide demonstration (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:33)
GUIDE_STROKE_SECONDS=1.4 s and GUIDE_REST_SECONDS=0.5 s for the repeating guide cycle (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:34-35)
TAP_ASSIST=0.22 lane progress per assisted tap; no source-defined total completion time (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:17-20)
timing.assumptions: The guide-cycle values describe code timing, not a measured child's play session. Completion time depends on how many deliberate strokes/taps and approach actions are needed. The helper's wall time is probe execution time and is not gameplay duration.

tactile.target_size: The probe's synthetic live-fixture metadata resolves to 151.25×207.5 canvas units (scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:40-43,211-215), about 50.4 units wide per lane. Source assigns a lane by dividing the fixture into thirds (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:436-440). The probe does not measure projected phone hit geometry; the per-lane width is below the DL-UI-03 110-unit guideline and merits a phone-size comfort check.
tactile.press_response: A lane press starts the scrubber affordance and hides the idle guide; with the actor bound it requests approach, and a tap is armed to award the 0.22 assist only after the contact action. Probe assertions for guide response and contact-gated tap passed (probe.log:35-36,119). Rendered-frame latency was not measured.
tactile.drag_hold_release: A downward drag reports partial wipe progress while moving through the lane; release under the 12-unit tap threshold uses tap assist, while a longer stroke arms its local action. No hold is required. The probe releases one synthetic downward stroke per lane and checks completion (probe.log:119-123).
tactile.ownership: The activity tracks one active touch ID and ignores events from other IDs for that gesture (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:230-247,266-268). This was exercised through direct handler calls in standalone contact-action cases, not a hardware multitouch stream.
tactile.cancellation: cancel_touch cancels the contact action and pending lane before releasing touch state (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:135-139,296-321). Probe retarget/focus-cancel assertions verified that unearned work did not award lane progress (probe.log:34-35). Pause/back/overlay teardown through the displayed application route was not tested.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: a child can choose among three visible strips and see the dirt wipe downward, while the small tap assist offers a less demanding alternative without making an unattended win. The source and probe support these mechanics; I did not see the rendered scene or observe a child.
play_appeal.variety: Within this focused activity, the mechanics vary between a full downward stroke and repeated lane taps, with a hand guide demonstrating the stroke. The intended variety and child preference are untested.
play_appeal.world_response: Code removes each dirty lane from the top and emits a progress mask; the cleanup controller persists the mask and announces lane cues, then advances to the seahorse stage when complete (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:450-472; scripts/games/day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:478-502). Probe verifies these state transitions, not their visual or audible quality.
play_appeal.replay: Source initializes lane progress from the saved clear mask and derives the next hint from uncleared lanes (scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:73-96,111-119). The probe exercises completion persistence/unlock, but does not perform a fresh visible re-entry route or child replay observation.

observations.title: Synthetic downward strokes clear all three lanes and advance the pool stage
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:223-258 sends a synthetic touch, two drag positions, and release through the waterfall handler for each of three lanes; it asserts partial top-down grime reveal and clear mask 0x07.
scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:260-264 asserts the saved waterfall mask, cleanup step, and seahorse as current activity.

audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L08/attempt_1/probe.log:119,121-123 reports guide display, partial wipe, three-lane clearing, and completion/unlock OK; final line is RESULT: PASS checks_failed=0.
observations.reproduction: Run the retained L08 receipt command. It exercises synthetic downward input on the fixture and asserts all three lane bits and the next stage.
observations.child_impact: Within the asserted setup, a downward stroke produces local visual progress and finishing all strips advances the activity. This supports a clear action/result relationship but does not show whether the image or response is legible to the child.
observations.proposed_repair: No defect established by this lane. Preserve the one-finger stroke and truthful top-down wipe while collecting routed visual evidence.
observations.acceptance_test: On the shipping renderer, enter the pool naturally, make a downward stroke on each visible lane, and verify local dirt removal, one appropriate lane cue, persisted progress, and the seahorse handoff after the third lane.

observations.title: Tap assist and actor-contact gates prevent a tap or released swipe from awarding remote work
evidence: scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:296-333 routes a short tap through TAP_ASSIST or arms the longer drag callback; _finish_tap_lane and _finish_drag_lane apply progress only after the callback.

scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:742-763 checks that cancellation awards nothing, a same-lane retap does not restart work, a tap earns one assist after local scrub, and a quick released swipe completes after contact.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L08/attempt_1/probe.log:34-38 reports the retarget, cancel, local scrub, contact-wait and release checks OK.
observations.reproduction: Run the L08 receipt; the standalone waterfall contact-action segment drives touch begin/end and contact-action processing, then checks progress before and after the approach/work completes.
observations.child_impact: The mechanics are designed to let a brief tap still help while requiring the character's local action before credit, and interruption does not pay unearned work. Actual character/tool readability and perceived wait remain unobserved.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated by this probe. Retain contact-gated assist and interruption semantics; assess their visible timing on device.
observations.acceptance_test: With routed one-finger input on device, compare tap and stroke response; verify the action appears at the waterfall before progress is credited, lane retarget/cancel clears pending work, and another touch cannot steal the gesture.

observations.title: Each lane's nominal hit strip is narrow relative to the child-target guideline
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:40-43 sets fixture art bounds to 121×166 and the expected live bounds at :211-215.
scripts/games/day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:20 defines ART_TO_STAGE=1.25 and :593-599 derives the fixture size from source_art_rect, yielding 151.25×207.5 and nominal lane width about 50.4.

scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:436-440 divides the fixture into three lane hit regions; design/06_COMPREHENSIVE_DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md:714-716 says required touch targets should be at least 110×110 base-canvas pixels or provide an equivalently generous projected hit region.
observations.reproduction: Use the fixture geometry in the probe and follow _waterfall_fixture_size plus _lane_at: 151.25 canvas units total width divided into three nominal columns, each approximately 50.4 units wide.
observations.child_impact: A narrow horizontal lane may be harder for a preschooler to hit reliably on a phone, particularly when the lanes are visually adjacent. This is a geometry-based concern, not a demonstrated miss or defect; projected hit testing and child comfort have not been observed.
observations.proposed_repair: Measure the displayed hit region on the target phone and test child-sized finger tolerance. If lane selection proves difficult, consider a generous lane-aware tolerance that still makes each visible strip own its input without neighboring ambiguity.
observations.acceptance_test: Measure projected lane hit areas and spacing at phone size, then verify intentional taps/strokes on each strip register reliably without cross-lane selection under one-finger child play.

observations.title: The passing contract probe does not prove the castle-to-waterfall route or ordinary input dispatch
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:29-64 constructs ReefMain and a Control host, creates synthetic waterfall and seahorse sprites, assigns them into the room-item dictionary and calls cleanup.setup directly.
scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:235-256 calls waterfall_activity._gui_input directly with constructed InputEventScreenTouch and InputEventScreenDrag objects.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L08/attempt_1/receipt.json records headless=true and rendered_mobile_acceptance=false; the retained log records the scripted PASS at line 123.
observations.reproduction: Read the probe setup and direct calls cited above; its runtime does not load a full displayed pool route or inject through normal GUI dispatch.
observations.child_impact: The probe cannot show whether a child discovers the waterfall after skimming, sees the lane cue at phone size, or can reliably touch the intended lane through normal event routing.
observations.proposed_repair: No production repair is inferred. Keep this evidence gap separate and collect a routed, displayed phone session before claiming route or tactile acceptance.
observations.acceptance_test: From a fresh save, enter the dirty pool through its visible route, complete skimming, observe the waterfall cue, use ordinary touchscreen input on all lanes, and verify completion/re-entry on the target Android device without adult prompting.

strengths.claim: The lane interaction pairs an authored hand demonstration with a top-down removal of the dirty strip, giving the child a visible example of the intended downward stroke.
strengths.evidence: scripts/games/pool_waterfall_activity.gd:563-582; scripts/probe_day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:223-251; runtime log:119,121. The probe verifies visibility/state, not rendered composition.

strengths.claim: Tap assist is bounded at 0.22 progress and unearned actor work is canceled or retargeted without awarding the old lane.
The same waterfall progress signal is connected to the cleanup controller's persistence and lane voice-cue path, with completion advancing only from the waterfall phase.
strengths.evidence: scripts/games/day_one_pool_cleanup.gd:379-389,478-502; runtime log:122-123. Probe state wiring does not establish audible voice or real save-device behavior.

acceptance_gaps: No fresh-save castle entry or complete skimming-to-waterfall route was played through ordinary displayed input; this probe directly constructs the controller and directly calls _gui_input.
No rendered Mobile capture verifies the waterfall cue, scrubber contact, hand guide, lane separation, or visible action timing at supported aspect ratios.
Nominal lane width from the probe fixture is about 50.4 base-canvas units; no Lenovo Tab M11 projected hit-area or finger-tolerance measurement exists in this review.
No target-device latency, frame pacing, thermal/memory or audio audibility evidence; no observed-child comprehension, comfort, agency, session length or fun evidence; no owner acceptance.
